nodes.claim: The gradient-square terms arise because x_t is output before loss l_t is known; they become non-positive if l_t is observed before producing x_t. Explicit forward reference: Section 15.5.1.
V is convex iff lambda*x+(1-lambda)*y is in V for x,y in V and 0<lambda<1.
dom f={x:f(x)<+infinity}; indicator i_V is 0 on V and +infinity off V. The source permits extended-real-valued functions.
Convexity means convex epigraph. A convex function has convex domain; i_V is convex iff V is convex; convex f+i_V is convex when V is convex.
For f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity] with convex domain, convexity is equivalent to the two-point convexity inequality on dom f.
Nonnegative linear combinations of convex functions are convex. The proofs of the operations listed here are left as exercises at the top of printed11.
Convex f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity], differentiable at x in int dom f, satisfies the global affine lower bound.
V nonempty convex, x* in V, f convex and differentiable over an open set containing V. Then x* minimizes f on V iff <grad f(x*),y-x*>>=0 for every y in V.
Theorem 2.7 plus the nonnegative inner product implies f(y)>=f(x*) on V.
A negative directional derivative along feasible segment z(alpha)=alpha*y+(1-alpha)*x* gives a smaller objective for sufficiently small positive alpha, contradicting minimality.
A function f:R^d->[-infinity,+infinity] is closed iff every sublevel {x:f(x)<=alpha}, alpha real, is closed.
In Euclidean spaces, closed iff lower semicontinuous.
i_V closed iff V closed.
Proper means nowhere -infinity and finite somewhere.
i_V proper iff V nonempty.
For proper f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity], g in R^d is a subgradient at x when f(y)>=f(x)+<g,y-x> for every y in R^d.
partial f(x) is the set of all subgradients; subdifferentiable at x means partial f(x) is nonempty.
For proper convex f, dom partial f is a subset of dom f and includes int dom f. The relative-interior strengthening is explicitly not used in this book.
f:R^d->R, V convex, and nonempty partial f(x) for every x in V imply restriction of f to V is convex. The codomain in the printed statement is R, not extended reals.

nodes.region: Theorem 2.21 first proof paragraph and two inequalities
nodes.claim: For x1,x2 in V and lambda in [0,1], take y=lambda*x1+(1-lambda)*x2 in V and g in partial f(y). Apply its global support inequalities to x1 and x2.
Multiply support inequalities by lambda and 1-lambda, add and cancel inner products to get convexity on V.
f:V->R, V convex; strict inequality at nontrivial convex combinations of distinct points defines strict convexity.
Strong convexity implies strict convexity. For differentiable strictly convex f, f(y)>f(x)+<grad f(x),y-x> for x!=y.
psi:X->R strictly convex, differentiable on nonempty int X, X=dom psi; B_psi:X times int X->R; B(x;y)=psi(x)-psi(y)-<grad psi(y),x-y>.
For y in int X and all x in X, B(x;y)>=0, with equality only when x=y. The first argument need not be interior.
For x,y in int X and z in X: B(z;x)+B(x;y)-B(z;y)=<grad psi(y)-grad psi(x),z-x>.
